verdicts.evidence: H1 on /dashboard/barn/extensions reads exactly "Extension Studio".
The .studio-home__lede under the title row reads verbatim: "Describe what you want in plain language; the assistant builds it against this Rancher. Nothing reaches users until you publish."

[data-testid=studio-count] read 3 with three rows. Typing "demo" in the filter left one row and the pill read 1; typing "zzzznope" left none and it read 0; clearing brought all three back and it read 3 again. After I created a fourth extension it read 4.

Typed "demo" into .studio-home__search-input: rows went from [base, demo, nodehealth] to [demo] and the count pill followed to 1. Typed "zzzznope": no rows survived (count 0), so it really removes as well as keeps. Cleared it and all three came back.
Clicked [data-testid=studio-crumb-extensions]: landed on /dashboard/c/local/uiplugins#installed, Rancher's own Extensions page. The crumb is an <a>.
.studio-home__crumb-current is a <span> reading "Studio" with no href. Clicked it: the URL stayed /barn/extensions.

The sixth .studio-home__th has empty text, no .studio-home__sort glyph and aria-sort="none"; the five columns before it all carry the glyph. Its cells hold the Review button plus the per-row overflow trigger.
Clicked the Name header: [base, demo, nodehealth, v6r] ascending, aria-sort="ascending"; clicked again: [nodehealth, demo, base] descending, aria-sort="descending".

With four rows of two different states, ascending gave [base Unsaved, nodehealth Unsaved, demo Live, v6r Live] and descending reversed the groups to [demo Live, v6r Live, base Unsaved, nodehealth Unsaved]. That is STATE_ORDER (attention first), not the badge word alphabetically, and the tie inside each group breaks on name so the order is stable.

First click gave aria-sort="descending" and the order [base 2 min, demo 2 min, nodehealth 5 hours]; second click gave "ascending" and [nodehealth 5 hours, demo, base]. Sorting on the rendered string would have put "2 min ago" first in ascending order, so this is sorting on the timestamp behind it. The cells also carry a title with the real reason ("An uncommitted file was edited then. The last commit is older.").
Ascending put nodehealth ("catalog · v0.1.0", installed) above base and demo ("local (preview)"); descending reversed it. That is the documented order (installed, then previewing, then neither).

The header is a live sort control: clicking it moved aria-sort to "ascending" then "descending" on that column only, and moved the .studio-home__sort--on glyph onto it. The row order did not change because all four extensions in this instance are Studio-authored with no repository, so sortValue returns the empty string for every one of them and the name tiebreak keeps the order. No repo-backed extension exists here to show a visible reorder.

Every row leads with an .s-badge. Observed two real states side by side: base/nodehealth "Unsaved" as s-badge--warning and demo/v6r "Live" as s-badge--success, and the extension I created flipped Live -> Unsaved as soon as a file changed in its pod and back after a revert. Building, Published, Failed and Draft did not occur in this instance.

Each name cell carries a second muted line that tracks state: "3 changes waiting for your review" / "2 changes waiting for your review" on the Unsaved rows and "On main, nothing uncommitted" on the Live ones. It changed as I added and reverted files in a pod.

All four rows read "Created here · no repo yet" with the sparkle, which is true - none of these extensions has a GitHub annotation. No repo-backed extension exists in this instance, so the "owner/repo - branch" half could not be observed.

nodehealth reads "catalog · v0.1.0" (it is the only one installed as a UIPlugin, at that version); base, demo and the extension I created read "local (preview)" (pod running, not installed). Every extension here has a live pod, so the dash placeholder for one running nowhere still could not be observed.

Cells read "1 min ago", "2 min ago", "5 hours ago". The extension I created showed "5 min ago" five minutes after creation and its cell carried the hint "An uncommitted file was edited then. The last commit is older.", so the value is read from the pod rather than from page load.
Clicked the name cell of a row: landed on /dashboard/barn/editor/<that extension>.
base and nodehealth (both with uncommitted work) each show a secondary "Review" button, [data-testid=studio-review-<name>]. Clicked the one on base: /dashboard/barn/extensions/base/review.

The last cell is .studio-home__td--actions holding the Review button plus an overflow trigger. Opened it on an extension I created: five items - Open in the workspace, Review changes (disabled, "none"), Open files, Open the brief, Remove the local install (disabled, "not installed"). Drove three: /barn/editor/<ext>, /barn/extensions/<ext>/files, /barn/extensions/<ext>/brief. On base "Review changes 3" was enabled and went to /barn/extensions/base/review; on nodehealth "Remove the local install v0.1.0" was enabled, which matches the only installed UIPlugin (not clicked - it changes the Rancher everybody shares).
Clicked the primary "New extension": /dashboard/barn/extensions/new.

The neutral GitHub-marked button in the title row is labelled "Import". Clicked it: the ImportExtensionModal opened, headed "Import an extension from GitHub" with "Step 1. Connect GitHub" and the repository form.

Clicked [data-testid=notifications-center] on /barn/extensions: the notification centre opened, headed "Notifications / Mark all as read" with real entries from this session ("Interrupt sent ... Escape went to the session").

[data-testid=header__brand-img] is a bare ; img.closest("a") is null. Clicked it from /barn/extensions and the URL stayed /barn/extensions (same on all five screens I drove). Rancher shell chrome, not pkg/barn.

verdicts.evidence: /barn/extensions/new renders one centred bordered .new-ext__card whose .new-ext__title reads "New extension".
.new-ext__lede reads verbatim: "Describe what you want in your own words. The assistant writes the code, runs it against this Rancher, and shows you the result before anything is shared."
The first .new-ext__label above the description textarea reads "What should it do?".

On load document.activeElement is the .new-ext__prompt-input textarea (autofocus). Its placeholder is the worked example from the design. I typed a description, submitted, and the text arrived verbatim in the created extension's BRIEF.md under "## What you were handed" and on the brief screen.
SLabel "Try" renders to the left of the three chips in .new-ext__examples.

Clicked the "a cost report per namespace" chip on an empty form: the description became "Add a cost report per namespace." and the Name field filled with "cost-report-per". With "Seed text" already in the field the chip appended rather than replaced: "Seed text a cost report per namespace".
Clicked the "a Longhorn volume health tab" chip: the description became "Add a Longhorn volume health tab." and Name filled with "longhorn-volume-health".
Clicked the "a fleet drift dashboard" chip: the description became "Add a fleet drift dashboard." and Name filled with "fleet-drift-dashboard".
Both lines render above the outcome field: the label "What can someone not do today?" and the hint "The question a ticket usually skips."

A sparkle-marked .new-ext__note under the outcome field reads "Answer this and the assistant can tell you when your description is a solution rather than a problem - which is most of the time, and is where the rewrites come from."

Typed a problem statement into the outcome field and submitted: it reached the created extension's BRIEF.md under "## The problem" verbatim and the brief screen rendered it under "What you said a good outcome would be". The pushback half is real machinery but cannot complete here - the brief's callout offers "Ask it to argue with this" and the pod's claude has no credential, so it answers "Not logged in - Please run /login", which the card says up front rather than pretending.
Both lines render above the four cards: "Where should it appear?" and "This decides the parent route - the single hardest thing to fix later."

On load [data-testid=new-ext-placement-cluster] "Inside a cluster / Cluster nav, below Storage" is the only card with aria-pressed="true". Clicking another card moved the selection and clicking back returned it. I created an extension with this placement selected: its product.ts in the pod is the cluster shape - inStore: "cluster", showClusterSwitcher: true, HOME_ROUTE "<name>-c-cluster-home" - with the comment naming the explorer nav, and its BRIEF.md records "Parent route: `c-cluster`" and "Inside a cluster - cluster nav, below storage. Registered in `product.ts`."

Clicked [data-testid=new-ext-placement-global] "Top-level nav / Its own entry in the global menu": aria-pressed moved to it and off all three others, and clicking "Inside a cluster" moved it back. The generated code for this placement is the global shape (extension-placement.ts writes inStore management with route params { cluster: "_" }); whether it then appears in the running global menu is not observable until the extension is published, which I did not do.

Clicked [data-testid=new-ext-placement-resource] "On a resource / A new tab on a resource detail page": it became the only card with aria-pressed="true" and a follow-up appeared - "On which resource?" with [data-testid=new-ext-resource] and the hint naming node / pod / apps.deployment. Selecting any other card removed the follow-up again.

Clicked "Not sure yet / Let the assistant pick and explain": only that card selected. It is the placement that produces "Parent route: `undecided`" in the brief with the paragraph telling the assistant to choose between c-cluster, root and resource-detail and say why, seeded as a top-level entry meanwhile - so the decision is genuinely deferred and written where the assistant reads it.

Typing "Show longhorn volume capacity trends per node" put "longhorn-volume-capacity" in the Name field unprompted. Editing it to "my-own-name" stopped the suggestion overwriting it - retyping the description left the edited value alone. And the edited value is what gets built: I typed "v6r" over the suggested "v6r-audit-probe" and the extension created was named v6r (Deployment/Service/ConfigMap barn-v6r-extension, package pkg/v6r in the pod).
The SField under Name renders the hint "Suggested from your description - editable".

[data-testid=new-ext-target] reads "Build and preview against / local - v1.36.1+k3s1" and both halves are real readings of the local cluster. But it is a <div class="new-ext__box new-ext__box--static">: it contains no select, input or button, and clicking it opened nothing (0 poppers, listboxes or selects appeared). The design draws a cluster picker; the product ships a static readout and says why in the hint.
verdicts.defect: The design draws a cluster picker and the product ships a static readout. Honest (every extension pod lives in the local cluster) but the promised control does not exist - a design decision rather than a code fix.

verdicts.evidence: [data-testid=new-ext-target-note] under the target box reads "Changes only ever run here until you publish. Not a choice, and nothing to choose from: this is the only cluster this Rancher manages, and every extension pod the Studio creates lives in it."

A grey .new-ext__git panel with the GitHub mark reads "No GitHub connection needed to start. You can connect one later when you want to keep the source or publish to the catalog." And the claim holds: I created an extension end to end with no GitHub token configured in this Studio.

Clicked "Connect GitHub" inside the git note with "keepme text" in the description: the EditorSettingsModal opened ("Connect GitHub / Used to clone repositories when you import one, to push when you publish ... "). Closing it left the description still reading "keepme text".

verdicts.evidence: On /barn/extensions/base/files the masthead reads "base" over the eyebrow "Files"; on the extension I created it read that extension's name, so it is the route parameter and not a hardcoded string.

With uncommitted work in base the masthead badge read "Unsaved"; the extension I created read "Live" with a clean tree, flipped to "Unsaved" the moment I appended to three files in its pod, and back to "Live" after I reverted them.
The masthead SChip reads "main" with the branch icon, which is what `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` reports in the pod.

The branch row at the top of the tree column is an SMenu: clicking .files__branch opened a list, and with one branch in the pod the single item read "main / checked out". Its subtitle is honest about what it can say - "1 branch in the pod · sync with origin is not read here" - rather than inventing an ahead/behind count. Only one branch exists in these pods, so switching to a different one could not be driven.

[data-testid=files-review-changes] read "Review 3 changes" with three uncommitted files, "Review 2 changes" after I reverted one and plain "Review changes" on a clean tree - the count tracks the pod. Clicking it went to /barn/extensions/base/review.

[data-testid=files-publish] is disabled with nothing to publish and enabled with changes. Clicked it on base: the publish flow opened - the PublishModal headed "Publish base", explaining that the package is built in its pod and this Rancher pointed at the result, with the destination rows and their gates. Cancelled rather than publishing into a Rancher four other verifiers share.
Clicked the chevron button[aria-label="Back"] at the start of the masthead: left the Files screen for /dashboard/barn/extensions.
Clicked the overflow at the right end of the masthead: a menu with "Refresh the tree", "Copy this file's path", "Open the workspace" and "Review changes <n>" (the count matching the tree).

The four-tab strip switches the surface and the underline: Assistant -> /barn/editor/base?tab=assistant with the conversation, Changes -> /barn/extensions/base/review with the change list ("Changed files 0 / Nothing has changed"), Terminal -> /barn/editor/base?tab=terminal with the live terminal, Files -> back here. On each destination aria-selected is true on exactly the tab clicked (.s-tab--selected), and on the Files screen itself it is Files.

On a clean tree the Changes tab reads "Changes" with no badge. I appended to three files in the pod and it read "Changes3"; reverting one through the UI took it to "Changes2"; reverting the rest took the badge away again. The number matched `git status --porcelain` each time.
The first .files__panel-title in the tree column reads "Files", above the branch row, the filter and the tree.

Clicked product.ts in the tree: the editor header title, the provenance line, the code pane and the "Where used" panel all switched to product.ts and the --current highlight moved off the previously open file. Repeated for Home.vue, BRIEF.md, index.ts, CLAUDE.md, package.json and l10n/en-us.yaml.
Clicked the "pages" folder row: Home.vue disappeared from the tree (16 rows to 15); clicked again and it came back (16). Same for the other folders.

With base's tree holding one added and two modified files, the tree showed HARNESS.md with a "new" badge and BRIEF.md and product.ts with "edited"; untouched files carried none. When I appended to package.json and tsconfig.json in another pod they gained "edited" badges on the next load, and after a revert the badge went.

The control at the right of the FILES heading opens a two-item menu: "Name / folders first, then A to Z" and "Changed first / uncommitted files at the top · current". Choosing "Name" moved BRIEF.md (edited) out of its position above .gitignore and down into alphabetical order; choosing "Changed first" put it back at the head of the loose files. So the order really changes.

The header names the open file and [data-testid=files-provenance] states its provenance, and it changes per file: index.ts "Last commit by barn, 2 days ago · 14 lines · committed", product.ts "... 42 lines · uncommitted changes", pages/Home.vue "... 46 lines · committed", BRIEF.md "Last commit by barn, 19 hours ago · 36 lines · uncommitted changes". The line counts and the commit state match the pod.

The pane renders numbered .files__code-line rows with a .files__ln gutter starting at 1, and .files__tok spans for keywords, strings and markdown headings. LOSSLESS CHECK (regression): I read the rendered line text back for nine files - index.ts, routing/index.ts, product.ts, package.json, CLAUDE.md, BRIEF.md, .gitignore, vue.config.js, l10n/en-us.yaml and pages/Home.vue - and compared it byte for byte against `cat` in the pod. Every one matched exactly, same line count and same content per line (14, 16, 42, 20, 97, 36, 1, 1, 2 and 46 lines). The highlighter loses nothing.

Opened CLAUDE.md (97 lines): .files__code has scrollHeight 2330 against clientHeight 383, so it scrolls internally. Set scrollTop to 600 and it moved to 600 while the editor header, the tree column and the "Where used" panel all stayed at the same viewport top (160px before and after).

With product.ts open, clicked [data-testid=files-ask-about-file]: the app moved to /barn/editor/base?tab=terminal, the workspace with this file handed to the assistant. The turn it sends carries the file - the activity stream in that pod holds earlier turns of exactly this shape, "Context: pages/W5Probe.vue. ..." and "Read product.ts in this package and explain it ...", stamped "Sent from the workspace screen by Default Admin".

The pane is read-only until Edit. Clicked [data-testid=files-edit]: it became a [data-testid=files-edit-area] textarea. Appended a marker line and pressed Save; `grep` in the pod found the marker in the file and `git status` showed it modified. Save is disabled while the draft equals the file, so a no-op cannot be saved.

Appended to package.json in a pod, opened it and clicked [data-testid=files-revert]: a confirm appeared ("package.json goes back to its last commit ... Only this file. Nothing else in the working tree is touched"). Confirmed: in the pod `git status` lost package.json (the two other modified files stayed), the appended line was gone from the file, and the tree badge and the Changes count both dropped by one.

The right-hand panel is headed "Where used" and its contents change per file: for pages/Home.vue "Where it surfaces ... Home.vue is mounted at /<ext>/c/local/home, read out of routing/index.ts"; for product.ts "product.ts does not render a page of its own. Only the components named in routing/index.ts have a route"; for index.ts the CLAUDE.md references. It is a reading of the file, not a fixed block.

The reference list is labelled "References to <basename>" (SLabel), under the "Where used" section heading, and the label changes with the open file. The design's wording is "Referenced by"; the product names the file in the heading instead.
With pages/Home.vue open the only reference row was "routing/index.ts:3 imports it". Clicked it: the editor header, the code pane and the tree selection all moved to routing/index.ts.

Each row carries a reason read off the matching line, not just a path: "routing/index.ts:3 imports it - import Home from '../pages/Home.vue';" for Home.vue, "CLAUDE.md:19 describes it in a table" for product.ts, two CLAUDE.md rows for index.ts. The panel says what it is - a fixed-string search, with "mentions it" when the line shows no relationship - rather than claiming a symbol index.

With pages/Home.vue open the panel offers "Show the running extension"; clicking it framed a real 307x192 iframe at /k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-<ext>-extension:8005/proxy/ - I read the document inside the frame and it is the extension's own dev-server dashboard, not a fixed image. verdicts.evidence: DRIVEN END TO END this round, on extensions nobody else was using. Working: with a probe line in product.ts I clicked [data-testid=barn-rollback] ("Roll back to the last commit") and got "Rolled back to the last commit / The tree as you left it was snapshotted first, so nothing is lost." The pod's tree really went back (the probe line was gone), a refs/tags/barn-snap/<ts> "the failed build before rolling back" appeared, the failure card disappeared and the badge went Failed -> Unsaved. MANDATORY SAFETY SNAPSHOT: I then made the place the snapshot has to be written unwritable in the pod (a regular file at .git/refs/tags/barn-snap, so `git tag -f barn-snap/<ts>` cannot create the directory - verified directly in the pod, exit 128) and clicked it again. It refused: "The roll back did not happen / Nothing has been rolled back. The tree could not be snapshotted first, and the Studio will not replace a tree it cannot put back: the snapshot of <ext> failed in the pod (exit 1): fatal: cannot lock ref ...". HEAD and the working tree were byte-identical before and after, the failure record was still in sessionStorage and the failure card was still on screen. Repeated on demo as instructed, with a durable refs/barn/working-build ref in place so the button read "Roll back to the last working build": same refusal, demo's HEAD and its modified product.ts untouched, failure record not cleared. Everything I broke was put back afterwards (demo: tags dir restored, working-build ref deleted, product.ts checked out, and `git tag` verified working again).

Same action, second affordance, and they run the same roll-back.ts. Driven for real: toast "Rolled back to the snapshot ... The tree as you left it was snapshotted first", the pod's tree restored to that point, a second safety snapshot written, the failure record cleared and the badge back to Unsaved. With the snapshot blocked it refused with git's own reason and nothing moved, on both the extension I created and on demo.

.queue__lede under the title row reads "Nothing in this list is live. Everything here is still running only in its author's preview, and you are both its author and its only reviewer, so nothing here is waiting on anybody else. A change is only a review request once it has been handed over as a packet; until then it is its author's own work and it is not in this list at all."

The sparkle-marked .queue__footnote-text at the end of the list reads "Rows lead with what the change is for, taken from its brief - not with a file count. A change with no brief says so, which is the point: a reviewer should never have to reverse-engineer intent from a diff."

"Waiting on you" is the selected tab on load (aria-selected="true"), its badge read 1 and the list under it held exactly one card. When I handed a second extension over the badge read 2 and two cards rendered; when that change moved to the outcome sign-off the badge went back to 1 and the card left this tab. The count and the list agree.

Clicked it: aria-selected moved to it and the list changed. With nothing half-answered it read 0 and showed the empty state "Nothing is waiting on anybody else / A change appears here once you have answered one of its two questions and it is still not through the gate." After I approved the code on my own extension and handed the approved commit over, the badge read 1 and the row appeared here - a real state transition, not a static filter.

Clicked "Signed off this week": aria-selected moved to it, the other two lists went away and it rendered "Nothing signed off in the last 7 days / A change appears here once both questions have been answered against what was handed over - the code review and the outcome sign-off." Its window is the one the Review settings dialog sets (Count as signed off for N days).

Clicked the "Oldest first" control: a four-item menu - "Oldest first / by last commit · current", "Newest first / by last commit", "Most changes", "Least changes". With two rows in the queue, "Newest first" gave [my extension, base] and "Most changes" gave [base (2 files), my extension (0)], and "Oldest first" put base back on top - so the list really reorders and on the real value. The choice persists (it survived reloads); I set it back to "Oldest first", which is where I found it.

Each row's first line is a purpose sentence taken from the brief - base's reads "Mid-incident an operator cannot tell a spike in node pressure apart from a slow degradation, so they open Grafana or guess.", which is the opening of its BRIEF.md - and the second line is "<name> · <version> · packet <n>" followed by the diff size ("2 files · +17 -0 · 4 acceptance criteria"). An extension whose brief I emptied led instead with "No brief - nobody wrote down what this is for." rather than falling back to a diffstat.

Every row shows a "Waiting" label with a duration read from the hand-over time - "1 hour" on base, "1 minute" then "4 minutes" on the packet I created as time passed - and a requester line under it. base reads "nothing records who asked for this" (its BRIEF.md has no ## Who asked section, so the screen says so rather than naming whoever is looking); the extension I created through screen 02 reads "asked for by local://user-btc48", the principal its brief actually records.

Every row carries a risk chip plus a one-line rationale, and the rating tracks the tree rather than being fixed: base "medium" with its reason, my extension "none / nothing uncommitted" on a clean tree, "low" with one changed file and "medium" once 46 lines had changed. The design's em-dash placeholder for a blocked row is not what the product does - my blocked row still showed "medium" with "46 lines changed · ..." beside the Blocked chip. That is a real measurement of a real diff rather than a blank, so the promise's substance holds; only the mock's placeholder does not.

Judged against the corrected DEPARTURES.md #5 argument, not the old one. The corrected argument is right about the code: review-queue.vue models four parts (partFor(): blocked, handover, outcome, code) and chips three - I saw "Blocked" (lock) on a row whose brief I emptied and "Outcome sign-off" (eye) on a row whose code I had approved, and "Not handed over" has its own chip and testid. It is also right that the action button says which question is being asked: actionLabel() returned "Open the brief" on the blocked row, "Sign off" (primary variant) on the outcome row and "Review" on the ordinary one, all from one map. So the removal is defensible and the redundancy the design draws is real. It is still a fail against the promise as written, because the promise is that EVERY row says which kind of review is being asked and the ordinary code-review row - the common case, and the only one of the four with no chip - says it only in the verb on its button, never as the named readout ("Code review") the design draws. That is a deliberate, argued gap rather than a bug.
verdicts.defect: The "Your part" readout is rendered only for the exceptional parts. review-queue.vue chips part blocked, handover and outcome and has none for code, with the comment "a chip that says the same thing on every row is not a readout, which is why there is no \"Your part\" column here any more". On an ordinary code-review row the only thing naming the part is the word "Review" on the action button. DEPARTURES.md #5 argues the removal and the corrected argument survives scrutiny; keep this as a recorded departure rather than fixing it, unless the design owner wants the pill back on all four.
